title: Domain-fingerprint mini-bundles for calibration dataset curation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: design and produce compact, per-domain calibration mini-bundles (’mini-bundles’) derived from production prompts for FP8/INT8 quantization validation. These bundles should represent the domain distribution, preserve rare but important signal, be small enough to iterate quickly during quantization builds, and be deterministic and reproducible for regression testing. Deliver a sampling spec, generation tooling, and an initial curated dataset for 6 pilot domains (search, chat-assist, code-completion, summarization, support-FAQ, form-filling).
background: Current calibration collections are large and slow to iterate on. We need small, high-fidelity packs that reflect production prompt characteristics per domain: request lengths, token distributions, KV-cache behavior, prefix repetition, and rarity of tokens/entities. Existing tickets explore stratified reservoir sampling and cohort catalogs; this task consolidates those investigations into a repeatable mini-bundle pipeline optimized for quant builds and nightly accuracy checks.
proposed_solution: Produce deterministic mini-bundles per domain using a hybrid sampling algorithm: (1) fingerprint each prompt by hashing normalized prompt text + domain tag + context-length bucket, (2) assign a dynamic priority score combining recency, request frequency, and rarity-signal, (3) perform reservoir sampling per fingerprint with adjustable slot counts, and (4) enforce post-sampling constraints: max context-length coverage, max tokens per bundle, and de-duplication by semantic hash. Provide CLI and CI hooks to regenerate bundles and upload artifacts to the calibration artifact store.
sampling_protocol: 1) Ingest 14 days of production events (anonymized). 2) Normalize prompts (strip PII, canonicalize whitespace, remove transient ids). 3) Compute features: token_count, prompt_type, user_seen_count, cluster_id (from lightweight LSH), and novelty_score (TF-IDF rarity). 4) Bucket by domain and context-length (0-64,65-256,257-1024,1025+). 5) Within each (domain, bucket, cluster) run weighted reservoir sampling with weight = alpha*recency + beta*frequency + gamma*novelty (alpha=0.6,beta=0.3,gamma=0.1 initial). 6) Promote top-N rare exemplars per domain (N configurable). 7) Trim bundle to target size (e.g., 500 prompts) using priority and diversity heuristics.
calibration_pack_schema: Each mini-bundle is a newline-delimited JSONL file with fields (id, domain, context_tokens, prompt_text_hash, normalized_prompt, source_date, priority_score, cluster_id, provenance_link). Bundles have a manifest JSON with metadata (generated_at, filters_applied, sample_seed, hash_of_bundle). All fields are required for CI reproducibility.
validation_plan: - Unit tests for normalization and fingerprinting. - Offline simulation: apply proposed sampling to 30 days of historical data and compare statistical moments (token length distribution, top-100 tokens coverage) to production baseline. - Quantization sweep: run FP8 and INT8 calibration using the mini-bundles and compare perplexity and end-to-end metric deltas against a held-out larger calibration set. - Regression monitoring: nightly job will compute calibration drift (KL divergence on token distribution) and accuracy regressions on canonical prompts.
instrumentation_and_metrics: Metrics emitted during bundle generation: input_event_count, unique_fingerprints, selected_count, average_priority, duplication_rate, bucket_coverage_ratio. Validation metrics: KL_token_dist, avg_perplexity_delta_FP8, avg_perplexity_delta_INT8, failure_rate_in_quant_tests. Expose metrics to console-calibration dashboard and alert when KL_token_dist > 0.15 or avg_perplexity_delta_INT8 > 2.0.
rollout_plan: 1) Generate pilot bundles for 6 domains and run local quant experiments (week 1). 2) Review with Applied ML and Runtime teams; iterate sampling weights (week 2). 3) Add CI job to regenerate bundles weekly and run quant validation on PRs touching quant code (week 3). 4) If metrics stable, adopt mini-bundles as default quick-validation artifact and keep larger packs for final regression runs (week 4+).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: overfitting to small bundles may miss rare failure modes. Mitigation: maintain two-tier calibration: mini-bundles for fast iteration + larger periodic full-run packs. Risk: PII leakage from upstream. Mitigation: enforce strict normalization and PII filters; run a K-anonymity check before producing bundles. Risk: deterministic hashing could leak user ids if canonicalization buggy; mitigation: unit tests and stakeholder review of normalization code.
open_questions: What is the authoritative domain taxonomy—do we need subdomains or feature flags?
Should promotion of rare exemplars be per-customer or global?
What is the storage TTL for mini-bundles in the artifact store?
Do we include model-generated assistant completions or only user prompts?
notes: Design review requested with Applied ML (Marco, Priya) and Runtime (Ethan) scheduled for 2026-03-15.
Early experiments show reservoir+rarity preserves top-500 token coverage with only 20% sample size vs baseline.
Need sign-off from Privacy on normalization transform; flagged as pre-merge check.
Consider adding lightweight semantic dedup via minhash if duplication_rate > 5%.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic bundle generation CLI that accepts seed and outputs bundle + manifest.
Pilot bundles for the 6 pilot domains generated and uploaded to calibration-artifacts with manifest.
Offline distribution checks pass: token length and top-100 token coverage within 10% of production baseline.
Quant validation job using bundles produces avg_perplexity_delta_INT8 <= 2.0 and KL_token_dist <= 0.15 for at least 4 of 6 domains.
Privacy review completed and normalization tests present in CI pipeline.
